lines.en: “I'm Dokja.”
I really do introduce myself to people this way, and it often leads to the following misunderstanding.
“Oh, you must be an only child?”
“I am an only child, but that's not the Dokja I mean.”
“Sorry? What do you mean, then?”
“My name is Dokja. Kim Dokja.”
Kim Dokja (金獨子).
My father gave me that name so I would become a man who was strong even on his own.
But thanks to the name my father gave me, all I've become is an ordinary, lonely, single man.
Basically, it goes like this.
Kim Dokja. 28 years old. Single.
Hobby: reading web novels on the subway home from work.
“At this rate, you'll fall right into your smartphone.”
A noisy subway.
I looked up reflexively. Eyes brimming with curiosity were looking straight at me.
It was Yoo Sangah, an employee in Human Resources.
“Oh, hello.”
“Heading home from work?”
“Yes. You too, Yoo Sangah-ssi?”
“I got lucky. Our department head is away on business today.”
The seat beside me happened to open up, and Yoo Sangah plopped down. A faint fragrance drifted from her shoulder, pressed close to mine, and I found myself tensing up.
“Do you usually take the subway?”
“Well, the thing is.......”
Yoo Sangah's expression darkened. Come to think of it, this was the first time I'd run into her on the subway home from work.

That made sense. From Assistant Manager Kang in Human Resources to Department Head Han in Finance. Everyone at the company had heard the rumor that men lined up at the end of every workday to drive Yoo Sangah home.
But what Yoo Sangah said was unexpected.
“Someone stole my bicycle.”
Bicycle?
“You were cycling to and from work?”
“Yes! I've been working so much overtime lately that I feel like I'm getting less and less exercise. There were some other things bothering me, too, so it served both purposes.”
Aha, so that was it.
Yoo Sangah smiled brightly. Seeing her this close, I could understand a little of how those men felt, pining after her, but it had nothing to do with me.
Everyone's life has its own predetermined genre, after all, and Yoo Sangah was living in a different genre from mine.
Once the awkward conversation ended, we each looked at our phones. I reopened the novel app I'd been reading in earlier, and Yoo Sangah...... what was that?
“¿Puede prestarme dinero?”
“Sorry?”
“It's Spanish.”
“......I see. What does that mean?”
“It means, ‘Please lend me some money.’”
Yoo Sangah answered confidently.
Studying even on the subway home from work.
Definitely a different genre from mine.
But where was she planning to use a phrase like that once she'd memorized it?
“You're working hard.”
“What are you so absorbed in, Dokja-ssi?”
By the time I thought ‘Oops,’ Yoo Sangah's gaze had locked onto my smartphone screen.
“Is that a novel?”
“Yes, well...... you could call it studying Korean.”
“Oh, I like novels too. It's been a while since I've had time to read any, though......”
That was unexpected.
Yoo Sangah liked novels?
“Haruki Murakami, Raymond Carver, Han Kang.......”
Of course, I thought.
“Which authors do you like, Dokja-ssi?”
“You probably wouldn't know them even if I told you.”
“I've read quite a lot of novels, you know. Who's it by?”
At times like these, reading web novels is a really awkward hobby to have.
I glanced at the title of the novel displayed in the app.
『The Sekai After the Fall』.
Author: Sing Shang Shong
Whatever else I might do, I couldn't say, “I'm reading The Sekai After the Fall by Sing Shang Shong.”
“It's just a fantasy novel. You know...... what's it called. Something like The Lord of the Rings.......”
Yoo Sangah's eyes widened.
“Aha. The Lord of the Rings. I've seen the movies too.”
“The movies are good.”
A brief silence followed. Yoo Sangah was still looking at me and seemed to be waiting for me to say something.
This was getting uncomfortable.
I decided to casually change the subject.
“It's already been a year since we joined the company. It was around this time last year. Time really flies.”
“It really does. Neither of us knew anything back then, did we?”
“That's right. It all feels like yesterday, and the contract period is already almost over.”
It wasn't until I saw Yoo Sangah's expression that I realized I'd picked the wrong subject.
I'd forgotten.
That last month, Yoo Sangah had already been promoted to a permanent position in recognition of her work with a foreign buyer.
“Oh, that's right. I'm late congratulating you. Sorry. Haha, I should've worked harder on my foreign languages too.”
“Oh, no, Dokja-ssi! You still have your performance review, and.......”
I hated to admit it, but Yoo Sangah looked impressive as she spoke.
A face shining brightly, as though all the world's spotlights were trained on a single person.
If this world were a novel, someone like her would be the protagonist.
Really, it was only natural.
I hadn't made an effort.
Yoo Sangah had made an effort.
I'd read web novels.
Yoo Sangah had studied.
So it was only natural that Yoo Sangah would become a permanent employee and my contract would be terminated.
“Um...... Dokja-ssi.”
“Yes.”
“If you'd like...... could I tell you about the app I use?”
For a moment, Yoo Sangah's voice sounded distant.
A feeling of drifting endlessly away from the world.
To keep my mind from floating away, I forced my eyes to focus and stared straight ahead.
A boy was sitting in the seat across from me on the subway.
Had he just turned ten or so?
Holding an insect net in one hand, the boy sat beside his mother, smiling innocently.
“......Dokja-ssi?”
What would it have been like to live a different life?
I mean, if my life had belonged to a different genre.
“Kim Dok.......”
If the genre of my life had been ‘fantasy’ instead of ‘realism’.......
Could I have been the protagonist?
I didn't know.
I would probably never know. But if there was one thing I could know, it was this:
“It's all right, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“Sorry?”
“Even if you tell me about that app, it won't do any good.”
That the genre of my life right now was unmistakably ‘realism.’
“Dokja has a reader's life, after all.”
“Sorry? What do you.......”
“Some people are just like that.”
And that in this genre, I was a ‘reader,’ rather than the protagonist.
“A reader's life.......”
Yoo Sangah looked serious, so I waved a hand to show that I really was all right.
I couldn't be sure, but she must have been sincerely worried about me. She did work in Human Resources...... she would already know how I'd been performing.
“You really say such wonderful things, Dokja-ssi.”
“Sorry?”
“Then I have Sangah's life to live.”
As though she'd made up her mind about something, Yoo Sangah went back to studying Spanish. I watched her for a moment, then returned my gaze to my web novel.
Everything had gone back to normal, but strangely, I was having trouble scrolling down through the novel.
Perhaps the weight of reality, brought home to me anew, had fastened itself to the bottom of the scroll.
That was when a notification appeared at the top of my smartphone.
[You have 1 new email.]
The sender was the author of ‘Ways of Survival.’
I opened the email right away.
―Dear reader, the paid service begins at seven this evening. This will help you. I wish you success.
[1 attachment]
Come to think of it, the author had said there would be a gift.
Was this the gift?
......I really must be a reader by nature. Getting this excited over a single email.
Right, living as a reader wasn't all bad.
First, I checked the time.
The paid service was supposed to begin at seven, so there were exactly 5 minutes left.
I opened my favorites list in the novel app.
I was the only reader, after all. Leaving the first congratulatory comment ought to give the author some encouragement.
―This work does not exist.
I typed ‘ruined’ into the search box several times, but the result was always the same.
The page for Ways of Survival had vanished without a trace.
That was strange. Did a novel's page ever get deleted without notice just because it was switching to paid access?
At that moment, the subway lights blinked out, plunging the interior into darkness.
Screeeeeeech!
The train lurched violently, letting out a metallic shriek. Yoo Sangah gave a small scream and grabbed my arm.
I heard the passengers stirring uneasily.
Yoo Sangah was gripping my arm so hard that the pain in my left arm drew more of my attention than the force of the sudden stop.
The train came to a complete stop some ten seconds later. Confused voices erupted all around.
“Huh? What's going on?”
“What? What's happening?”
One by one, smartphone screens lit up in the darkness. Still clutching my left arm, Yoo Sangah asked.
“Wh-what do you think happened?”
I spoke, putting on an air of calm.
“Don't worry. It's probably nothing serious.”
“You think so?”
“Yes. At worst, it's probably a suicide scare. The driver will make an announcement soon.”
No sooner had I finished speaking than the driver's announcement came over the speakers.
―Attention, all passengers aboard this train. Attention, all passengers aboard this train.
The noisy surroundings fell quiet. I spoke as though breathing a sigh of relief.
“See? Nothing serious, right? Now they'll apologize, and the power will come back.......”
―E-everyone, run...... everyone......!
What?
A shrill screech followed, and the broadcast cut out. The train descended into chaos.
“D-Dokja-ssi? What on earth.......”
A blinding light flashed in a carriage ahead. Then came the sound of something bursting, and a noise like a large drum being torn apart.
Something was approaching us through the darkness.
It was pure coincidence that I looked at the clock at that moment.
With a tick, it felt as though the world had stopped.
Then I heard a voice.
[The free service for planetary system 8612 has ended.]
[The main scenario has begun.]
It was the moment the genre of my life changed.
「It's a dokkaebi. Someone said that when it first appeared.」
I didn't know why that sentence suddenly came to mind.
A subway train that had stopped abruptly.
A carriage with no power.
There weren't enough details to warrant déjà vu. Sudden subway stops were rare, but they did happen from time to time.
Even so, why?
The opening of a familiar novel kept coming back to me.
But that made no sense.
There was no way, was there?
That was when the front door of carriage 3807 flew open and the power returned. Beside me, Yoo Sangah murmured.
“......A dokkaebi?”
A buzz rang through my head―. The novel I knew overlapped with the reality before me, and everything around me trembled uneasily.
「Two small horns. Draped in a little straw mat, a strange creature covered in soft down floated in midair.」
「Too bizarre to call a fairy, too wicked to call an angel, and too innocent in appearance to call a devil.」
「And so it was called a ‘dokkaebi.’」
And I already knew the first words that ‘dokkaebi’ would say.
Fiction and reality overlap exactly.
“What's that thing saying?”
“Is this augmented reality?”
Amid the passengers' murmuring, I felt as though I alone had been thrown into another world.
That was unmistakably a ‘dokkaebi.’
The very dokkaebi that had ushered in tragedy throughout thousands of installments of Ways of Survival.
...Yoo Sangah's voice broke me out of my thoughts.
“It sounds a little like Spanish. Should I try talking to it?”
Somewhat dumbfounded, I asked.
“......Do you even know what that is? Are you going to ask it to lend you money?”
“Well, no, but.......”
That was when clearly enunciated Korean reached our ears.
[Ah. Ah. Can you hear me? Honestly, what a hassle. The Korean language patch wasn't installed. Everyone. You can hear me, right?]
Was it because they were hearing a familiar language? I could see the tension leaving people's faces. The first to step forward was a large man in a suit.
“Hey, what do you think you're doing?”
[......Pardon?]
“Are you filming a movie? I have an audition, so I need to get going.”

His face was unfamiliar, so he seemed to be an unknown actor. His voice was so full of spirit that if I'd been a casting director, I would've hired him on the spot. Unfortunately, though, the being before him was no director.

[Ahh, an audition. I see. You have auditions at this hour too. Haha, I didn't do enough research. I was sure they said the most people would follow if the paid service began around seven in the evening.]
“What? What are you talking about?”
[Now, now, everyone. Calm down, take a seat, and listen to me, please. I have something important to tell you!]
My chest feels tighter and tighter.
“What's going on! Get the train moving!”
“Someone contact the driver!”
“What do you think you're doing without getting the public's cooperation!”
“Mom, what's that? A cartoon?”
There was no doubt.
This was the sequence of events I knew.
I had to stop them.
But there was no way.
There was no chance people would listen to a cute little bundle of CGI.
The only thing I could do was stop Yoo Sangah, who was about to get up without knowing any better.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi, it's dangerous. Stay where you are.”
“Sorry?”
Startled, Yoo Sangah opened her eyes wide. I'd blurted it out, but I had no way to explain what I understood was happening.
To be precise, I didn't need to explain.
[Haha, you really are noisy.]
Because a being more persuasive than anyone else was right there before us.
[I told you to be quiet.]
The dokkaebi slowly closed its eyes, then opened them. Their glow had turned red.
Something cracked in a rapid series of pops, and silence washed over the train.

A large hole had opened in the forehead of the unknown actor who'd said he needed to get to an audition. His mouth opened and closed a few times before his eyes went blank and he collapsed where he stood.
[This is not a film shoot.]
Once again came a sound like a gourd splitting open. This time it was the woman who'd been going on about the driver.
[Nor is it a dream. Nor a novel.]
One, two. Jets of blood sprayed into the air as people's heads began to burst.

The people who'd protested to the dokkaebi. The people screaming and making a scene. Holes were being punched through the heads of everyone who showed even the slightest sign of making a disturbance. In an instant, the train became a sea of blood.
[Nor is it the ‘reality’ you knew. Do you understand? So everyone shut up and listen to me.]
At least half the people were dead.
A subway train on the way home from work, strewn with blood and pieces of corpses.
People no longer screamed. Like prehistoric apes facing a powerful predator, they all stared at the dokkaebi in terror.
I held my breath, pressing firmly down on Yoo Sangah's shoulder as she hiccupped repeatedly in shock.
This is real.
It hadn't felt real when the strange messages sounded in my ears, or when the dokkaebi appeared before my eyes. As I looked at the blood-soaked carriage, that sense of reality was finally awakening.
[Everyone, life has been pretty comfortable for you until now. Hasn't it?]
The priority seats. An old woman who'd met the dokkaebi's eyes was wetting herself.

[You've lived for free for far too long. Life has been too generous, hasn't it? You've been breathing, eating, shitting, and breeding however you please since the day you were born, without paying a thing! Ha! You really have been living in a fucking wonderful world!]
For free. No one on this subway home from work had lived for free.
A place for people who worked desperately to earn money and survive. That was what this subway home from work was.
Even so, at that moment, no one could challenge the dokkaebi's words.
[But the good times are over now. You couldn't expect to enjoy everything for free forever, could you? If you want happiness, it's only common sense to pay for it. Isn't it?]
The gasping passengers couldn't answer. But then. Someone cautiously raised a hand.
“D-do you perhaps want money?”
I wondered what kind of person could spout something like that at a time like this. To my surprise, it was a face I knew.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi. Isn't that Department Head Han from Finance?”
There was no doubt. The company's prime example of someone hired through connections, and the number 1 boss new employees tried to avoid. Han Myungoh, head of the Finance Department.
What on earth was that man doing on the subway?
“If it's money, I'll give you as much as you want. Please, take it. For your information, th-this is who I am.”
As Department Head Han boldly produced even his business card, people looked at him with encouragement. It felt as though they were watching a savior stand up to a terrorist.
“How much will it take? One big one? Or two?”
It was far too large a sum for a mere department head at a subsidiary to throw around so casually.

There had once been a rumor that Department Head Han Myungoh was the company chief's youngest son, and I found myself thinking it might be true. A mere department head couldn't be carrying that many checks in his wallet.
[Hmm, so you're offering me your money?]
“Y-yes! I don't have much cash on me right now...... but if you let me out of here, I can give you as much as you want.”
[Money, yes, that's nice. Plant fibers imbued with the intersubjective agreement of many humans.]
Department Head Han's face brightened at those words. His expression said, ‘See, money solves everything.’ Poor man.
“Th-this is all I have on me right now, so at least take this―”
[That only applies within your own spacetime.]
“Pardon?”
The next moment, flames sprang up in midair. Every check in Department Head Han's hand caught fire. Horrified, he screamed.
[That kind of paper has no value in the macro-dimensional realm. Try that again and I'll make your head explode. Keep that in mind.]
Fear spread across people's faces again. Their expressions were like novels where you could tell what came next, making their thoughts easy to read.
「What on earth is about to happen?」
And I alone knew what would happen next.
[Whew, your debts are piling up even while we stand here talking. Well, all right. Rather than explaining a hundred times, it would be quicker to let you earn some money yourselves, wouldn't it?]
The dokkaebi's horns lengthened as though they were antennae, and its body floated up toward the train's ceiling.
Then, a moment later, a message sounded.
[Channel #BI-7623 has opened.]
[Constellations (星座) are entering.]
Small windows appeared above each of the people blinking blankly.
[The main scenario has arrived!]
<Main Scenario # 1 ―Proof of Value>
Category: Main
Difficulty: F
Clear condition: Kill one or more living creatures.
Time limit: 30 minutes
Reward: 300 coins
Failure: Death
Its body turning transparent, the dokkaebi gave a faint smile as it vanished into the next carriage.
[Well then, good luck, everyone. Please show me an entertaining story.]
Episode 1. Paid Service Begins (3)
After the dokkaebi disappeared, people reacted in different ways. Some tried desperately to escape the train, while others called the police. Yoo Sangah was among the latter.
“The police, the police aren't answering! What do we do, what do we do.......”
“Calm down, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
I looked straight into Yoo Sangah's unfocused eyes as I spoke.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi. You've played the game our development team just made, right? You know, the one where the whole world is ruined and only a handful of people survive.”
“Sorry? Why are you suddenly.......”
“Think of it this way. We're inside that game now.”
Dazed, Yoo Sangah moved her lips.
“It's simple. Don't freeze up. Just do what I tell you. Understand?”
“O-okay. What should I do?”
“Stay exactly where you are. Don't move.”
With those final words, I slowly brought my own breathing under control.
I needed time to properly take all of this in, too.
『Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World』.
Descriptions that had existed only in the novel were now being sketched from life (寫生) before my eyes.
「A dokkaebi with its antennae extended.」
「Corpses strewn about the carriage like garbage.」
「An office worker trembling, covered in blood.」
「An old woman groaning in the priority seats, having wet herself.」
I examined each of those scenes closely. Like Neo in The Matrix, questioning reality (實在).
I observed, doubted, and finally accepted it. I had no choice but to admit it. I didn't know why. But there was no doubt.
‘Ways of Survival’ had become reality.
Think.
About what I had to do to survive in this new world.
“Now, now, everyone! Calm down. Start by taking a slow, deep breath.”
Someone stepped forward exactly 5 minutes after the dokkaebi had disappeared.
Hair cut in a short two-block style.
He was a sturdy man, about a head taller than the average person.
“Have you calmed down? Please stop what you're doing and give me your attention for a moment.”
The people sobbing or talking on their phones lowered their voices. Once he had everyone's attention, the man with the two-block haircut spoke again.
“As you know, during a national disaster, a small disturbance can lead to a great loss of life. Therefore, I will take charge of the situation from this point onward.”
“What? Who the hell are you!”
“A national disaster? What kind of bullshit is that!”
Some people who'd finally recovered their senses stood up, fiercely objecting to the words ‘take charge.’ The young man took an official identification card from his wallet and showed it to them.
“I am an army first lieutenant currently serving in Unit 6502.”
Relief flickered across some of their faces. “A soldier. He's a soldier.” But it was too early to feel relieved.
“I received a message from my unit just a moment ago.”
People crowded around the soldier's smartphone. I happened to be nearby, so I could read it without difficulty.
―A Level 1 national disaster has occurred. All personnel are to report to their units immediately.
Gasps sounded all around.
A national disaster.
I wasn't surprised, since I'd already expected it. What surprised me was something else.
Army First Lieutenant Lee Hyunsung.
So this was that ‘Lee Hyunsung.’
I knew him. This was my first time seeing his face in person, but his name was clear in my mind. Naturally enough: he was one of the major supporting characters in Ways of Survival.
「Steel Sword Emperor Lee Hyunsung.」
Now even a character from the novel had appeared. I really had no choice but to accept the situation.
“Hey, soldier! What the hell is going on?”
“I'm trying to contact my unit as well, but.......”
“What about the Blue House! What are they doing! Contact the president, now!”
“I'm sorry, but I'm a junior officer. I don't have a hotline to the Blue House.”
“Then how do you expect to take charge!”
“This is all for your safety.......”
Watching Lee Hyunsung respond calmly even to that barrage of absurd questions, I was realizing anew that the novel's descriptions had been accurate.
But had Lee Hyunsung originally been introduced like this?
The question flashed through my mind, bringing an uneasy premonition.
As the sole reader of Ways of Survival, I could guarantee that Lee Hyunsung's first appearance had never been like this.
He first appeared in the story after the first scenario had ended, at the earliest.
......Then what was this?
My thoughts suddenly grow confused. If I could read ‘Ways of Survival’ again, I could get a clearer picture.
“The prime minister's speech is up! They say it really is a Level 1 national disaster!”
At someone's shout, everyone switched on their smartphones. Yoo Sangah turned her screen toward me.
“......Dokja-ssi, look at this.”
There was no need to enter a search term. ‘Prime minister's speech’ was the number 1 trending search on every portal site.
Of course, I already knew what was in that video.
―My fellow citizens, I have an announcement for you. Unidentified terrorists are currently active in Seoul and other unspecified areas.
The speech was simple.
The current administration would use every means at its disposal to fight the terrorists, and there would be no negotiations. All citizens should therefore rest assured and go about their work.......
I hadn't thought much of it when I'd read it in the novel, but actually hearing those words left me somewhat dumbfounded.
Terrorism.......
Right, it would be easier to think of it that way.
“But where's the president? Why is the prime minister giving the speech?”
“They say the president's already been taken out.”
“What? Really?”
“It's not confirmed, but in the Naver comments―”
“Fuck, then it's just hearsay!”
Of course, I knew it wasn't hearsay.
“Aaaagh! What the hell!”
People dropped their phones as gunshots rang out all around. The shots were coming from inside the smartphones.
A crackle of static, and a screen stained blood-red. Only a moment later did people realize what had happened and gasp.
“The p-prime minister.......”
The prime minister was dead.
With the prime minister's head bursting live on air, no less.
A few more gunshot-like sounds rang out, and then the scene on the screen fell quiet. A dokkaebi appeared on-screen next.
[Everyone, I told you. This isn't child's play like ‘terrorism.’]
Speechless, people opened and closed their mouths like stupid goldfish.
[You still haven't understood? This won't do. Does this still feel like a game to you?]
The voice was so relaxed that it felt all the more ominous. My fists clenched without my realizing it.
[Haha, my research says people in this country are good at games. Shall we raise the difficulty a little, then?]
With a beep-beep, a huge timer appeared in midair. The remaining time began to drop rapidly at that same moment.
[The remaining time has been reduced by 10 minutes.]
[Time currently remaining: 10 minutes.]
[If the first killing does not occur within the next 5 minutes, all living creatures in the carriage will be exterminated.]
“Wh-what does that mean? This is a joke, right?”
“Did you hear that message? Hey, did you hear it too?”
“Hey, soldier! What are we supposed to do now? Why aren't the police coming!”
“Everyone, please calm down for a moment and listen to me―”
With a few words from the dokkaebi, the situation in the carriage had escalated beyond anything Lee Hyunsung could bring under control. I felt Yoo Sangah clutching my collar tightly.
And I still couldn't shake the feeling that something about this situation was wrong.
Lee Hyunsung, a supporting character, had appeared.
So why hadn't ‘that guy’ shown up?
According to the story I knew, he should have appeared by now.
“Th-there's been a murder in the carriage behind us!”
Through the window by the connecting passage, we could see carriage 3907 turned into a sea of blood. Those who met the eyes of the killers in that carriage went pale.
“We can't let them in! Don't let anyone come through!”
People clung to the metal door. But it was unnecessary. The enemy hadn't been over there in the first place.
[All forms of entry and exit are restricted until the carriage's scenario is complete.]
As the message sounded, people were thrown back from the metal door as though they'd struck an invisible barrier.
“Wh-what's happening?”
Then the dokkaebi's voice sounded once again.

[Haha, some places have become quite entertaining, while others haven't even started yet. All right, here's a special service. I'll show you what will happen to you if nothing happens within the next 5 minutes.]
Something like a huge screen appeared in midair inside the train.
The place that appeared on-screen next was a classroom.
High school girls trembling in navy-blue uniforms.
A high school boy muttered, biting his nails.
“...Those are Taepung Girls' High School uniforms, aren't they?”
Beep-beep-beep-beep―an ominous signal rang out. The girls began to scream.
[The time limit has elapsed.]
[Payment settlement will now begin.]
No sooner had the announcement ended than the head of a girl sitting in the front row exploded.
One by one, then one by one again. Heads bursting here and there, scattering. Screaming, the girls ran toward the classroom door and windows.
“Ah, h-how could something like that―”
Cleaning tools broke and fingernails tore off, but the door wouldn't open. No one could get outside. Pop, pooom. The girls' heads kept bursting.
That was when one girl began strangling her friend.
A girl dying with a strangled groan.
And a moment later. The only one left on-screen was the last girl, looking around with venom in her eyes.
[Channel #Bay23515. Survivor of Taepung Girls' High School, Year 2, Class B: Lee Jihye]
The image of the girl glaring at the screen disappeared, and the dokkaebi's voice followed.
[Well? Entertaining, isn't it?]
The dokkaebi spoke with a smile, but people were no longer looking at the screen. Whenever their eyes met, they edged away from one another.
“What the fuck! What the hell is all this!”
Even Yoo Sangah released her grip on me. But she hadn't moved away from me yet.
With both hands free, I switched on my smartphone.
Why hadn't ‘that guy’ appeared yet?
A mixture of information I knew from the novel and information I didn't know.
The only way to get through this situation was to read Ways of Survival again.
But where on earth could I find that novel again?
A novel so unpopular that no one had even shared a pirated copy...... no, wait.
[1 attachment.]
Looking at the window on my smartphone, I went blank for a moment.
Surely...... it couldn't be?
A moment later, when I opened the email's attachment pane, bewilderment washed over me.
The attachment the author had sent was named as follows.
[Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World.TXT]
I let out a disbelieving laugh.
Thinking it couldn't be true, I rubbed my eyes and looked again, but there was no mistake.
The file extension was TXT.
So this person had just...... sent me a text copy of their own novel and called it a gift?
[You are acquiring an exclusive attribute.]
[The exclusive skill slot has been activated.]
Messages sounding in my ears as I opened the file.
If the world had changed into the world of ‘Ways of Survival,’ it was nothing to be surprised about.
Every survivor in Ways of Survival acquired an exclusive attribute and became physically capable of using exclusive skills.
I quietly repeated ‘Attributes Window’ in my mind. If I'd acquired an attribute, I needed to know what it was.
[The Attributes Window cannot be activated.]
What?
I called out ‘Attributes Window’ again, but the result was the same.
I was dumbfounded.
How could something like this happen?
If I couldn't use the Attributes Window, I couldn't know what attributes or skills I had.
They said knowing yourself and your enemy meant winning a hundred battles out of a hundred, but here I was, unable to know even myself, let alone the enemy.
After glaring into empty space for a while, I gave up for the moment and decided to read the text copy the author had sent me first.
[Your reading speed increases due to the effect of your exclusive attribute.]
I didn't know what the attribute was, but perhaps thanks to its effect, it took me less than 1 minute to read the opening of ‘Ways of Survival.’
Found it.
My finger stopped near the beginning of the novel, at the scene where the protagonist was about to take a certain ‘action’ in his train carriage.
「He looked at the people gathered by the rear door of carriage 3707. The serrated wheel of the lighter gripped tightly in his hand was cold.
He would make no mistakes in this life. He would use any means necessary to achieve his goal.
The faces of people trembling in fear.
There was no guilt.
It would all be over in an instant.
He surveyed the people with a cold gaze. A moment later, a flame sprang up at his fingertips with a hiss. And everything began.」
A chill ran down my spine, and I had to read the passage several times. The reason for that sense of wrongness soon became clear.
Reflexively, I checked the number of the carriage I was in.
The carriage I was in was the one ‘directly behind’ the protagonist's carriage in the prologue.
My fingertips began to tremble faintly.
Then what had originally been destined to happen to the people in this ‘carriage’?

「Through the cloudy window, he looked into carriage 3807, which had descended into pandemonium. Was it already too late over there? It couldn't be helped. Only two people would survive in that carriage anyway.」
Only two would survive.
Everyone in this carriage would die except for two.
And I already knew who those ‘two people’ were.
Blankly, I raised my head and looked at Yoo Sangah.
This woman would probably die.
And so would I.
“Dokja-ssi, shouldn't we stop that?”
Something had already begun where Yoo Sangah was pointing.
A sobbing groan. An old woman curled up and a young man's savage face.
“Fuck, I already feel like shit, and this old bitch won't stop fucking sobbing! Will you shut up?”
The young man was the high school boy who'd been leaning near the entrance.
A slender build and hair dyed stark white. His name was written on the name tag attached to his uniform.
Kim Namwoon.
As expected, it was a name I knew.
「Lee Hyunsung and Kim Namwoon will probably be the only survivors in that carriage. It doesn't matter. Those two are the only ones I need anyway.」
“I told you to shut up, didn't I?”
Agitated, Kim Namwoon seized the old woman by the collar. Her feeble legs flailed. Kim Namwoon's palm traced an arc through the air.
Smack, smaaack. Smaaack.
Normally, anyone would have rushed over to stop him, but no one moved.
Before long, the slaps became punches.
“S-save me. Please, save meee......!”
I heard hard fists crushing frail flesh. Unable to bear the accusing looks, a few men hovered around Kim Namwoon, but no one would step in.
Unexpectedly, the first to roll up his sleeves was Department Head Han Myungoh.
“You little punk, how dare you treat an elder like......!”
But as he boldly stepped forward, as though to set an example, a mocking voice answered him.
“Ajusshi, do you want to die?”
“You still don't get what's happening?”
“What kind of bullshit is that, you ill-mannered little bastard!”
Despite Han Myungoh's curses, Kim Namwoon merely chuckled. He pointed at the train's ceiling.
“Can't you see that?”
Overhead, footage was playing on the holographic screen the dokkaebi had turned on.
[Save me, please save me!]
[Aaaaaagh!]
[Die! I said die!]
It wasn't just this train carriage or Taepung Girls' High School. Live footage of people dying all across the country. Kim Namwoon continued.
“You still don't get it? The army isn't coming to save us. And someone has to die.”
“Wh-what are you saying.......”
“We have to choose who's going to die.”
Unable to give a ready answer, Han Myungoh opened and closed his mouth.
The fine hairs were standing up on his exposed wrists, below his rolled-up sleeves.

“Of course I know what you're thinking, ajusshi. Killing your own kind to survive. Only fucking bastards do that. But listen, we don't have a choice. No choice. If we don't kill, we die. Who can blame us? Are you going to keep preaching about morals until you die?”
“Think carefully. The world you've known until now just ended.”
Han Myungoh's trembling shoulders.
It wasn't just Han Myungoh.
Cracks were spreading through the looks in people's eyes. The sight of a world built on vague notions of morality collapsing. And, as expected, it was Kim Namwoon who drove a wedge into those cracks.
“And a new world needs new rules.”
Kim Namwoon. The young man who adapted to the world of ‘Ways of Survival’ faster than anyone else.
Kim Namwoon turned back and resumed punching the old woman.
This time, no one stopped him. Neither Han Myungoh nor the other men...... not even Lee Hyunsung.
The soldier's tightly clenched fist trembled in the air, with nowhere to go.
He, too, had probably just made a choice.
“Whew...... I'm dead tired. How long are you all going to stand there watching? Do you all want to croak?”
People flinched at Kim Namwoon's ensuing rebuke.
Their naked expressions were as easy to read as sentences in a cheap pulp novel.
「If no killing occurs within 5 minutes, everyone in this carriage will die.」
The look in people's eyes was changing.
「If that old woman doesn't die, the one who dies in 5 minutes will be.......」
The most primal looks any living creature could have.
“Yeah...... that bastard's right. At this rate, we're all going to die.”
The first man ran toward Kim Namwoon. He rained kicks down on the old woman, who lay curled up on the floor.
“Have you all forgotten? Someone has to die! That's how we survive!”
“Ah, fuck...... I don't know anymore.”
Two, then three.
People who'd been standing there blankly approached the old woman.
The men who'd been hovering nearby like cowards, too.
The female college student who'd been recording a video on her phone, too.
The mother who'd cast her child aside, and even Department Head Han Myungoh, joining in late.
They were all beating the old woman, helping bring about her death.
“Die! Hurry up and die!”

They were like prison guards working together to execute a condemned prisoner. Like guards pulling their levers simultaneously so no one could know who'd killed the prisoner, they slowly killed the old woman with halfhearted kicks and punches.
And I was watching it all.
Like someone watching events unfold in another world, I stood by and let it all happen.
That nameless old woman had never been someone I could save.
She would have died in the original scenario too.
So...... standing by and watching her die was no sin.
That was when Yoo Sangah sprang to her feet.
“At this rate, she'll die.”
I reflexively grabbed her.
“I told you not to move without thinking.”
The arm in my grip was trembling. Clenching her fist as though to hide the trembling, Yoo Sangah spoke.
“I know, I know, but......!”
“If you go over there now, you'll die, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
Yoo Sangah's eyes were trembling with fear.
And yet.......
I realize it anew. Even when the genre of the story changes, some people still shine brightly.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi. Sit down.”
But Yoo Sangah isn't the person who can change this story.
Because she isn't the protagonist of this world.
“What? But―”
“Just do what I say this once. I won't interfere after that.”
After forcing Yoo Sangah back into her seat, I took a deep breath and turned away. As I straightened my back, my exhalation trembled faintly. I slowly loosen up my ankles and rotate my wrists.
Actually, it was a little early to step in. This hadn't been my original plan.
“......Dokja-ssi?”
Without answering her call, I looked at the people. People wholly absorbed in beating the old woman.
I hadn't stayed still all this time because I was afraid of Kim Namwoon or the others, or because I wholeheartedly agreed with their inhumanity.
I had simply been waiting.
For the moment when I needed to move.
In other words.
BOOOOM―!
Right now.
“Aaaah! What the hell!”
The explosion left my hearing muffled, and the train lurched to one side.
People screaming. Smoke rising from the carriage immediately ahead was drifting into ours.
It had begun.
He'd made his move.
I pushed off the floor with my right foot as hard as I could. Past the people collapsing with screams, toward the old woman.
“What the hell? Aaargh!”
Kim Namwoon collided with me head-on and tumbled to the floor with a shriek. At a glance, it looked as though I'd saved the old woman, but that wasn't what I was after.
Where?
I quickly scanned my surroundings.
People still kicking at the old woman even as the explosion knocked them down. In the middle of that hell, a child was crying.
It was the child who'd been holding the insect net earlier.
“Excuse me for a moment.”
I snatched the net from the child.
When I reached into the net, the unpleasant chitin of a grasshopper brushed my fingertips. I took one out and placed it in the child's hand. Then I turned toward the people.
“Everyone, stop. Killing that old woman won't save you.”
In the brief silence after the explosion, my voice rang out with surprising clarity. One by one, people began to look my way.
“Let's say you kill the old woman. What will you do next?”
It was satisfying to see their startled expressions. Shall I say a little more?
“If that old woman dies, it will count as the ‘first killing’ the dokkaebi mentioned, so you should be able to buy yourselves a little time. But what then?”
“If what the dokkaebi said is true, each of you will eventually have to kill one person. So who will you kill after the old woman? The person next to you?”
Only then did something occur to them. They looked at one another and hesitantly backed away.
Eyes filled with terror.
The truth was, everyone knew.
That the old woman was only the beginning.
It was Kim Namwoon who steadied the wavering crowd.
“Haha, what are you all worried about? We can just kill that guy next! Cowards. Stop worrying about your own turn before it even comes! The odds are fifty-fifty!”
I knew Kim Namwoon would say something like that. I cut him off with a casual wave of my hand.
“There's no need to take that gamble. There is a way for you to survive without becoming murderers.”
“What?”
“Wh-what is it?”
A loud stir among the crowd. I saw Kim Namwoon's expression twist.
“Have you forgotten? I don't believe the scenario's clear condition was ‘Kill a person.’”
Most people still looked bewildered, but a few looked as though they'd realized something.
[Kill one or more living creatures.]
That's right. The word ‘person’ had never been specified in the scenario's instructions.
Killing one or more living creatures.
Which meant that anything alive would do.
Someone quick on the uptake shouted, looking at the net in my hand.
“Insects! They're insects!”
Grasshoppers and crickets leaping about inside the net. People's eyes flashed. I nodded.
“That's right. Insects.”
I reached into the net and took out a grasshopper. It was the plump-bellied one I'd picked out beforehand.
“G-give me that! Hurry!”
“Just one! I only need one!”
Watching the people approach with outstretched hands, I slowly back away, one step at a time.
The explosive frenzy that had been aimed at killing the old woman was now directed at me.
A faint laugh escapes me.
Why? Even amid this precarious tension, why is my heart beating as though it were enjoying itself?
“Would you like them?”
I shook the net like a trainer taunting a pack of wild beasts. Just as a few impatient people got to their feet and were about to rush me.
“Then take them!”
I crushed the grasshopper in my hand.
[You have earned the ‘First Kill’ achievement!]
[You receive 100 coins as an additional reward.]
At the same time, I hurled the net in my other hand with all my strength. Specifically, in the exact opposite direction from where the old woman and the crowd were gathered in the aisle.
“You crazy bastard!”
Released into the air, the insects were leaping toward freedom with all their might.
Seeing the insects hopping all over the carriage, the people panicked.
“H-hey! Why would you do that―”
While the others could only stare in shock, a few quick-thinking people shoved past me.
“You'll pay for this, you fucking bastard.”
“......You'd better find them quickly. There are only 3 minutes left.”
At those words, the people began searching every nook and cranny of the subway seats like beasts that had lost their minds.
“Got one! Aaaaargh!”
The joy of those lucky enough to get an insect mingled with the malice of those attacking them, turning the carriage into a scene of chaos.
“Hey, why'd you do that? You could've just handed out the insects, couldn't you?”
I turned to find Kim Namwoon getting to his feet. Keeping a wary eye on the suspicious way he was stretching his neck, I answered.
“There are twelve people left in this carriage.”
“And there were three insects left in the net.”
Kim Namwoon looked blank for a moment, then burst into laughter.
“12 to 3? Hahahaha! You're right. So not everyone can survive anyway? That's why you threw it?”
“Yeah.”
“Bullshit.”
“Anyone with an ounce of common sense wouldn't do something like that for such a bullshit reason.”
The amusement on Kim Namwoon's face was growing.
“Be honest. Didn't you just want to watch that?”
I recalled the Kim Namwoon I knew from ‘Ways of Survival.’ It was then that a message sounded in my ears.
[The exclusive skill ‘Character List’ activates.]
Then, a window appearing before my eyes of its own accord.
I didn't know exactly what my attribute was, but looking at the list window before me, I felt I might have a rough idea.
<Character Information>
Name : Kim Namwoon
Age : 19
Constellation Sponsor (背後星) : None (Two constellations are currently showing interest in this individual)
Exclusive Attribute : Chuunibyou (General)
Exclusive Skills : [Unusual Adaptability Lv.3], [Knife Fighting (Knife fighting) Lv.1], [Blackening (黑化) Lv.1]

Most of the people with chuunibyou who appeared in ‘Ways of Survival’ couldn't endure the nightmare that had become reality and killed themselves. But the Kim Namwoon before me was different.
Kim Namwoon, the Delusion Demon (妄想惡鬼).
This young man, who would later be known by that nickname, wasn't an ordinary chuunibyou.
A young man who had long awaited nothing but the world's ruin, and so had adapted to this world at an ‘abnormal speed.’
“Let's team up. What do you say?”
That young man was now making me an offer.
[The character ‘Kim Namwoon’ expresses fondness for you.]
[Your understanding of the character ‘Kim Namwoon’ increases.]
If I joined forces with Kim Namwoon now, my immediate survival would probably be guaranteed.
If I hadn't read ‘Ways of Survival,’ perhaps my choice now would have been a little different.
“Sorry, but I prefer being alone.”
“Yeah? Hmm, that's a shame.”
Kim Namwoon smacked his lips lightly and stepped right up to me.
“Then how about getting out of my way? I've got business with the old hag behind you.”
At the words ‘old hag,’ I looked behind me. The old woman lay bleeding on the floor, barely breathing.
“What business?”
“You really have to ask?”
“Aren't you going to catch an insect?”
“An insect? Why would I catch that shit?”
Kim Namwoon gave a nasty smile.
“When there's a bug already caught right in front of me.”

I could feel Kim Namwoon's killing intent right in front of my face. A character who had existed only in the sentences of a novel stood facing me, his madness vividly real. Was that why? I couldn't help feeling a little impressed.
Kim Namwoon really was exactly the person I'd imagined.
[The affection of the character ‘Kim Namwoon’ for you decreases slightly.]
“What are you staring at? I told you to hurry up and move!”
“That might be difficult.”
“What?”
“I'm saying I can't let you through.”
“Haha, now you want to play at being some champion of justice? Got a split personality?”
I didn't answer. A dark shadow slowly spreading over Kim Namwoon's face. The eyes that had shone with affection were turning cold.
“No, wait. Did you throw the net over there because you were planning this all along? Seriously?”
“To save that old hag? Hahaha! Unbelievable! Seriously unbelievable! That's not it, right? Huh?”
I still didn't answer.
Seeing him this close brought old memories back to me.
“Well, turns out you're the kind of person I hate most. All you older fuckers really are the same.”
How much this bastard had driven me up the wall the whole time I was reading Ways of Survival.
[The character ‘Kim Namwoon’ despises you.]
“I told you to move, didn't I?”
I ducked, having timed it in my head. A fist flying at me before he'd even finished speaking.
“Oh? Not bad, huh?”
Even though I'd clearly seen it coming and dodged, a hot sensation lingered above my head. That hadn't been an ordinary punch.
[Blackening (黑靴) Lv.1]
A dark aura rising from Kim Namwoon's entire body.
It was an exclusive skill of the ‘Chuunibyou’ attribute.
Normally, unlocking a skill before the first scenario ended was rare, but Kim Namwoon was already manifesting one.
There was a reason the protagonist had recruited this guy despite his psychopathic personality.
THWACK!
The shoulder he'd struck went into a violent spasm. If I fight like this, I have no chance of winning.
......Should I use ‘that’ now?
Just as I was calculating the time in my head, a message sounded.
[Your understanding of the character ‘Kim Namwoon’ increases.]
[You are close to meeting the conditions for using Stage 1 of the exclusive skill ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint.’]
Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint?
Now what's this?
[You have met the conditions for using Stage 1 of the exclusive skill ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’!]
With a crash, Kim Namwoon's fist slammed into the floor.
“Haha, what the hell? I'm pretty strong, aren't I?”
A faint fist mark left on the carriage floor. Kim Namwoon, too, was now gradually realizing his own strength.
CRASH! CRASH! CRASH!
Blows powerful enough to break bones with a single hit kept pounding the floor. Kim Namwoon lashed out in apparent frustration.
“Ah, why can't I hit you!”
Of course he couldn't hit me.
It was all thanks to my second skill.
[Stage 1 of the exclusive skill ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’ activates!]
The moment the skill activated, I could tell exactly where Kim Namwoon's attacks were headed, as though I were reading his mind. For example, like this.
「Right flank」
I quickly stretch out and retreat into the attack's blind spot,
「Right eye」
then swiftly bend at the waist to evade the punches flying at me in succession.
“Seriously, I can't fucking land a hit!”
My poor coordination made counterattacking too much to ask, but I could at least evade most of his attacks.
「Left thigh」
This was enough to hold out.
What mattered was buying time.
Dodging Kim Namwoon's flying fists, I pointed to the clock hanging in the air.
“2 minutes left now, kid.”
Growing desperate, Kim Namwoon looked back and forth between me and the old woman.
“Fucking hell!”
At the moment of choice, Kim Namwoon's eyes settled on the old woman.
I had no choice but to grab the old woman and roll.
If the old woman died, Kim Namwoon would clear the scenario. No matter what happened, I couldn't let a bastard like him into the next scenario.
“Haha, I knew you'd move like that.”
Just as an ominous feeling struck me, Kim Namwoon was already pulling something out of his bag. The blade caught the white fluorescent light, stinging my eyes.
A pocket Swiss Army knife.
I'd forgotten. This guy was a hardcore military otaku.
SWISSSSH!
A combination of the technique skill [Knife Fighting] and the enhancement skill [Blackening].
The knife's target was clear.
「Heart」
An attack I couldn't dodge even knowing where it was headed. I make a quick decision. If I can't dodge an attack, it's better to take the hit. With as little damage as possible, if I can.
RIIIIIP!
Barely missing my heart, the blade sliced deeply across my shoulder.
It hurts. It really hurts.
So this was what it felt like to have my skin burn with pain. My vision wavered, and I felt death take a great stride closer.
“Haha, just die already!”
There was 1 minute and 30 seconds left until the scenario ended. I glanced at the old woman. I felt sorry for her, but now I truly had no choice but to use ‘that.’
“Kim Namwoon, second-year student at Cheongil High School. I have a question for you.”
“Are insect eggs ‘living things’ or not?”
I took the body of the grasshopper I'd killed earlier out of my pocket. Its egg sac was plump and swollen.
Fluid bursting out with a crunch.
An unpleasant wetness spread across my hand, and a message sounded.
[You have killed a living creature.]
[You receive an additional reward of 100 coins.]
[You have killed a living creature.]
[You receive an additional reward of 100 coins.]
Countless messages drumming against my ears.
Kim Namwoon frowned.
“Insect eggs? What the fuck are you talking about all of a sudden? Stalling for time?”
“You could say that.”
“How the hell would I know that? I always slept through biology.”
Looking at my blood-soaked shoulder, Kim Namwoon laughed as though he were enjoying himself.
“But there's one thing I know for sure. Know what it is?”
“What.”
“That you're gonna fucking die right now!”
Before I could answer, Kim Namwoon's Swiss Army knife moved. As expected, it was an attack that would be hard to dodge.
[You have acquired a large quantity of coins! Would you like to view the help guide for using coins?]
I skipped the explanations sounding in my ears. I knew it all already, so there was no need to listen.
“No, you're the one who's going to die.”
Even as I said those words aloud, I murmured something inwardly.
[Investing 2700 coins in ‘Constitution.’]
[Constitution Lv.1 -> Constitution Lv.10]
[Your Constitution level increases significantly!]
[Your body's durability increases significantly!]
Kim Namwoon's Swiss Army knife sank into the area around my heart.
More precisely, it looked as though it had.
Skin bearing only a scratch, as though the blade had scraped against solid rock. Kim Namwoon's eyes filled with shock.
“How!”
“I'll tell you the answer to that question. The answer is, ‘Eggs are living things.’”
“Wh-what?”
“And during its egg-laying season, a grasshopper lays 100 or more eggs at a time.”
Eggs. Living things. 100.
Unfortunately, there was far too little time left for a dim-witted high school boy to grasp what those pieces of information meant.
“What the fuck are you talking about!”
“I didn't expect you to understand. 1 minute left now.”
Only then did fear begin to show on Kim Namwoon's face.
“Aaaaargh! Die! I'll kill you!”
The path of the Swiss Army knife as it flew toward my neck. I deliberately left the attack unblocked.
SKRRRRAK!
Was it because this was a more vulnerable spot than my chest? The scratch was a little deeper than before, but it didn't hurt much.
“Kim Namwoon.”

Behind the desperately flailing Kim Namwoon, I could see people still searching for insects and grappling with one another. People who wouldn't hesitate to hurt each other if it meant their own survival.
“You were right earlier. I'm the same kind of person as you.”
Perhaps they were people I could have saved.
“What the fuck! Why won't you die! Why aren't you dying!”
55 seconds. 50 seconds. 45 seconds.
The knife kept leaving nothing but scratches.
Trickles of blood ran down, but the blade couldn't cut into the flesh beneath my skin.
Kim Namwoon spoke again with 30 seconds left.
He had dropped the knife and was kneeling before me.
“S-save me.”
25 seconds.
“I said, save me! Please! Please save me!”
“Why should I?”
20 seconds.
“H-human lives matter! That's just obvious!”
“That would be a rule of the ‘old world.’ You said it yourself. A new world needs new rules.”
10 seconds.
“No, no! I don't want to die! Aaaaaaah!”
5 seconds.
Kim Namwoon lunged at me with a shriek, aiming the knife at my eye.
At the very moment the blade was about to pierce my retina.

With a sputtering burst―Kim Namwoon's head exploded.

Heads bursting like fireworks heralding a new era.
I watched the scene with a little elation, a little guilt, and an inexplicable sense of disconnection.
Why?
How could I remain so calm, even as I watched that scene?
As though I were reading a novel.

An expression I'd never seen, despite having looked into countless mirrors.
I rubbed at the bloodstain near my cheek. It wouldn't come off. It turned out to be blood on the window.
Screeech.

Ahh.

The city in ruins amid gun smoke and dust.

And I was the only reader who knew how this world would end.
